skeleton.finalText:
I wrote `src/index.ts`, and `npm run build` finishes with no errors. The build also creates `src/index.js`; that's the compiler's output and `.gitignore` already excludes it. I didn't touch any other file.

The contract is one function plus two types:

- **`buildRequisitionsCsv(requisitions)`** returns the whole CSV as a string, with the byte order mark first. Its doc comment says it throws an `Error` naming the requisition's id in each bad-data case the spec lists. No time, key or randomness is involved, so nothing else needs to be passed in.
- **`Requisition`** is the input object: `id: string`, an optional `title` that may also be `null` (both count as missing), `status`, `openings`, `filled` and `createdAt: Date`.
- **`RequisitionStatus`** is the list of four valid statuses.

Decisions the test writers and the implementer should know about:

- **`status` is a plain `string`, not the four-status type.** That way a typed test can pass an unknown status without a cast. The doc comment points to `RequisitionStatus` for the valid values.
- **The creation time is a `Date`.** An invalid creation time means an invalid `Date`, such as `new Date("x")`, rather than a string that can't be parsed.
- **The id is a `string`.** The "then id" tie-break therefore sorts ids as text, not as numbers.

Exports: `RequisitionStatus`, `Requisition`, `buildRequisitionsCsv`

public.finalText:
I wrote the public test suite in `tests/public/requisitions-csv.test.ts`. `npm run build` reports no errors. All 12 tests run and fail, as expected: 11 with `not implemented`, and the refusal test because the error it gets (`not implemented`) doesn't name the requisition's id.

Each of the six scenarios has a happy-path test and a boundary test:

| Key | Happy path | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| `[happy-1]` | Requisitions given out of order come out by creation time; the exact output is checked, from the byte order mark to the final `\r\n` | Requisitions with the same creation time are ordered by id |
| `[happy-2]` | All four statuses, plain-digit numbers (including 0 and 1500), and a title that is `null` or missing | A creation time with a ±05:00 offset that falls on a different UTC date, and `23:59:59.999Z` |
| `[boundary-1]` | No requisitions gives exactly the byte order mark and the header row | The header ends with `\r\n` and no blank row follows it |
| `[boundary-2]` | A title with a comma or a double quote is quoted, with inner quotes doubled | `\n`, `\r`, a space at the start or end, and a title with only inner spaces (not quoted) |
| `[unhappy-1]` | A title starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` or a tab gets a leading `'`; `a=b` is unchanged | The quoting rule applies after the `'` is added (`\r` at the start, an inner `"`, a comma); a title starting with a space is not defused |
| `[unhappy-2]` | Each kind of bad requisition (unknown or wrong-case status, negative/fractional/NaN numbers, filled > openings, invalid date) throws an `Error` naming the bad requisition's id, even after a valid one | Filled equal to openings, and openings and filled both 0, are accepted; filled one above openings is refused |

Some assumptions the developer should know about:
- **Ids:** I used ids where any ordering method gives the same answer, because the spec doesn't say how ids compare.
- **Formula check:** it is applied only to titles, since the spec only mentions titles.
- **Build output:** the build also writes `.js` files next to the sources, including `src/index.js`. These are covered by `.gitignore`.

12 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
The private suite is in `tests/private/`, in four files.

- **`layout.test.ts`** covers `[happy-1]`, `[happy-2]` and `[boundary-1]`: file layout, row order, how values are written, and the empty file.
- **`fields.test.ts`** covers `[boundary-2]` and `[unhappy-1]`: quoting and formula defusing.
- **`refusal.test.ts`** covers `[unhappy-2]`: refusing bad data.
- **`timezone.test.ts`** covers `[happy-2]`: it sets `process.env.TZ` to UTC+14 and then UTC−12 inside each test and restores it afterwards. Without this, an implementation that writes local dates would pass whenever the grader's machine runs in UTC.

**Checks:**
- `npm run build` reports no errors.
- Against the stub, all 47 private tests fail and none crash.
- I wrote a reference implementation in a scratch copy outside the repo. It passes all 47 private tests and all 12 public ones.
- I also ran shortcut versions against both suites. Each one passes the public suite (or, for local dates, all but one public test) and fails at least one private test:
  - writing local dates instead of UTC dates;
  - looking up the status with `in` on a plain object, which accepts `"toString"`;
  - writing numbers with `String(n)`, which gives `1e+21`;
  - not padding the year to four digits (`999` instead of `0999`);
  - ordering by the written date, then id, instead of by the full creation time;
  - defusing more characters than the spec lists.

Two expectations are firm readings of the spec rather than restatements of it. Openings of 10^21 must be written as 22 plain digits. A year before 1000 must be written with four digits, as in `0999-04-07`.

The build writes compiled `.js` files into `src/` and `tests/`, so I deleted them. Only the `.ts` sources remain.

47 tests, in 4 files.

Open in the spec: none
